nodes.label: Content-Security-Policy
nodes.rationale: Defends against token theft via localStorage-based auth tokens and the app's contentEditable/innerHTML rendering of user-authored HTML; acts as a second line of defense behind the sanitiser. Fails closed: a mistake breaks the app rather than degrading security.

nodes.label: script-src 'self'
nodes.rationale: Load-bearing CSP line. No 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval', which is why the theme guard was moved from an inline script block to public/theme-init.js as a separate file. A bypass of the sanitiser then only injects inert markup instead of executing script.

nodes.label: style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'
nodes.rationale: The one real compromise in the policy: allows inline styles because Framer Motion animates via style attributes and the app sets colors from data. Exposure is smaller than script-src's because injected CSS can restyle but not read tokens.

nodes.label: connect-src 'self' https: wss:
nodes.rationale: Deliberately broad because the API origin is a build-time variable (VITE_API_URL); pinning it here would create lockstep-edit failure risk where every request gets blocked. https:/wss: still forbid plaintext exfiltration.

nodes.label: img-src / media-src allow https:
nodes.rationale: User uploads are served from Cloudflare R2 on a bucket-specific hostname configured outside this file; blob:/data: are needed by the client-side image downscaler before an upload is presigned.

nodes.label: object-src 'none', base-uri 'self', frame-ancestors 'none', form-action 'self'
nodes.rationale: The four directives that cost nothing: close plugin embedding, base-tag hijacking, clickjacking, and third-party form posts.

nodes.label: upgrade-insecure-requests
nodes.rationale: Belt and braces alongside HSTS.

nodes.label: Access/refresh tokens stored in localStorage
nodes.rationale: Accepted trade-off: the API and PWA are on different origins, so httpOnly; SameSite=None cookies are third-party and blocked by Safari/Chrome. Consequence: any script executing on this origin can read both tokens.

nodes.label: contentEditable + innerHTML rendering of user HTML
nodes.rationale: Described as the highest-risk pattern in the codebase; user-authored HTML is rendered into a contentEditable and mounted with innerHTML.
nodes.norm_label: contenteditable + innerhtml rendering of user html

nodes.label: Sanitiser (client + server)
nodes.rationale: A real sanitiser exists on both sides of the wire and is considered good, but is a single point of failure; CSP is the second point of failure behind it.

nodes.label: Strict-Transport-Security
nodes.rationale: Set for a year including subdomains; standard, and required for the HSTS preload list if ever wanted.

nodes.label: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
nodes.rationale: Stops a browser from deciding an uploaded file is HTML because it looks like it.

nodes.label: X-Frame-Options: DENY
nodes.rationale: Redundant with frame-ancestors for modern browsers; kept for older ones.

nodes.label: Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
nodes.rationale: Project ids live in URLs; this keeps them out of third-party Referer headers.

nodes.label: Permissions-Policy
nodes.rationale: Camera, microphone, geolocation and FLoC all off; the app asks for none of them.

nodes.label: Cache-Control on /assets/*
nodes.rationale: Content-hashed filenames make a year plus immutable safe.

nodes.label: Cache-Control on /sw.js
nodes.rationale: The opposite of asset caching: the service worker must always be revalidated, or a bad one pins itself.

nodes.label: Structural fix: httpOnly cookie on shared parent domain
nodes.rationale: The refresh token is still reachable by script on this origin. The real fix is moving it to an httpOnly cookie on a shared parent domain, requiring the API to be hosted at api.<same-domain> as the PWA. Until then, the CSP is mitigation, not cure.
nodes.norm_label: structural fix: httponly cookie on shared parent domain

nodes.label: <script src="/theme-init.js"> in index.html <head>
nodes.rationale: Palette and skin are applied before first paint via an external file rather than an inline block, specifically so the CSP in vercel.json can refuse script-src 'unsafe-inline' outright.

nodes.label: iOS standalone / viewport-fit=cover hints
nodes.rationale: viewport-fit=cover plus safe-area padding makes the standalone iOS window look native instead of letterboxed; apple-mobile-web-app-* meta tags are iOS standalone hints since Safari still ignores parts of the manifest.
